title: Jump-Diffusion Stochastic Quantization for Euclidean Lattice Field Theories
abstract: We construct the natural generalization of stochastic quantization (in the Markovian sense) by considering jump-diffusion processes. This class of stochastic processes exhibits non-continuous paths, so-called Lévy flights. In the presence of jumps, action landscapes with barriers can be efficiently explored, improving and even restoring ergodicity where traditional diffusion approaches become inefficient. We explore different strategies for constructing efficient jump updates, which we deploy to address the benchmark problem of topological freezing in 2d U(1) gauge theory.
summary: This paper extends stochastic quantization by incorporating jump-diffusion processes, allowing simulations to overcome topological barriers that trap standard diffusion methods. By developing rigorous mathematical constructions for the jump probabilities, the authors demonstrate a powerful tool to efficiently sample complex action landscapes in lattice field theories.
main_problem: To construct a natural generalization of stochastic quantization by incorporating jump-diffusion processes to efficiently explore action landscapes with barriers.
main_result: The framework successfully generalizes stochastic quantization by providing concrete, detailed balance preserving methods (additive proposals, invertible maps) for designing the necessary jump probabilities.
method: The authors derive and apply a generalized master equation for Poisson jump-diffusion processes, ensuring convergence to the desired equilibrium distribution $P(\phi) \propto e^{-S(\phi)}$ via specific construction strategies for the jump kernel.
model_or_system: The theory is applied to Euclidean Lattice Field Theories, using 2D U(1) gauge theory as a benchmark problem to address topological freezing. The dynamics are governed by a generalized Fokker-Planck master equation incorporating both diffusion and non-continuous jumps.
key_observables: Topological charge dynamics histogram, autocorrelation time reduction, and the acceptance rate of the jump process.
important_parameters: The jump rate ($\lambda_0$), the size/extent of the update ($L_w$), and the parameters defining the proposal distributions (e.g., $\sigma$ for Gaussian approximations).
main_assumptions: Boundary terms are neglected in deriving the Fokker-Planck equation; certain constructions rely on assuming measure-preserving maps whose inverses are also available.
figures_summary: Figure 4 compares topological charge dynamics histograms, showing that state-informed jumps (red bars) restore efficient transitions between topological sectors compared to uninformed updates (blue bars).
paper_structure: The paper first introduces the need for jump-diffusion processes over standard diffusion. It then derives the generalized master equation and presents three construction strategies (A, B, C) to enforce detailed balance in the jump term. Finally, it applies this framework to lattice gauge theory simulations, demonstrating improved sampling efficiency.
why_interesting: The rigorous mathematical development of ensuring detailed balance for non-local jumps is highly relevant to any simulation technique relying on Markov chain Monte Carlo (MCMC), including those used in quantum field theory or complex many-body systems where barriers are present.
